denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 30520 (septoplasty with or without cartilage scoring, contouring, or replacement with graft) with date of service 2026-04-01. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of medical management or an anatomic obstruction.

criteria.text: Nasal airway obstruction symptoms persisting for at least 3 months.
Failure of at least 6 weeks of an intranasal corticosteroid together with an oral or intranasal antihistamine.
Physical examination or imaging documenting septal deviation obstructing the nasal airway, with symptoms not explained by mucosal disease alone.

chart.text: Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

23 year old man here for nasal obstruction. Broke the nose playing ball as a teenager, never fixed. Discussed septoplasty, possible turbinate reduction, recovery of a week or so. His history otherwise: prediabetes, diet controlled, hypertension on lisinopril. Surgeries: appendix years ago. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 13 years ago, no alcohol, stays home with the kids. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Cannot breathe through the right side for going on 14 months, mouth-breathes at night, his spouse says the snoring is worse. Started him on fluticasone today, two sprays each side, see back in a few weeks. Anterior rhinoscopy: septum deviated to the right with a caudal spur contacting the inferior turbinate, right airway maybe 27 percent of the left. Turbinates decongest fine with oxymetazoline, the right side does not open up.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
CT sinus without contrast: rightward septal deviation with a bony spur abutting the right inferior turbinate, no significant sinus disease, no polyps.

Follow-up on the nose. Reviewed the imaging with him. Still wants to proceed. Vitals today 133 over 78, pulse 86. Says he used the spray for about a week and stopped because it burned. Has not tried anything else.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Blood pressure check. 136 over 91 today, 140 over 85 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
A1c came back 6.5. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 199, LDL 148, HDL 48, triglycerides 190. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 17 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.
He called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told him the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, he is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from his spouse.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Vitamin D came back 16. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Pre-op. Consent signed, septoplasty with possible inferior turbinate reduction. No aspirin for ten days.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-2 (medical) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan or a shortfall, not completed treatment or a met threshold.
